seed: A shape drawn with the Pen showed one row simply called Color, with no way to tell what that colour painted and nothing to say about the line itself. The walk draws a closed shape, asks it for an edge, and reads its Appearance beside an open one: the closed one's two colours are Fill and Outline, the open one's is Line, and under the line sit its thickness and what KIND of line it is - solid, dashed or dotted, what its ends look like and how its corners turn. It ends by switching the outline off and writing the whole thing out as SVG.

steps.note: a closed shape off the Pen arrives as its fill and nothing else, so the walk asks for an edge before reading the rows that describe one. That rule is path-arrives-with-no-edge-walk to prove; here it is only the starting point.
the inside painted a different colour from the line, so the two rows below plainly paint two different things

THE TEST: a closed shape's two colours are named for what they paint. Fill, then Outline with a switch on it, and under the outline its Thickness and what kind of line it is. Before this the second row was called Color and had nothing under it but a weight.
a closed solid shape has no ends anybody can see, so it is not asked about them. Corners and Pattern are both there, because both do something on a closed shape
THE TEST: the shape is dashed on the canvas, and because every dash has two ends the Ends row arrives directly under the control that just made it matter
round corners and square dash ends: three settings, three undo steps, all of them on the canvas
three undos put all three back, and the Ends row goes away again with the dashes that made it relevant

THE TEST: a shape with no outline offers to add one rather than showing dead controls. The switch is off and the colour, the weight and the line style are all gone with it, exactly as a switched-off Fill behaves
and one press brings the line back, at the weight a freshly drawn shape wears, wearing the colour it had before

THE TEST: an open path has no inside, so its one colour is called Line, the same word a line and an arrow use, and it carries no switch because taking its line away would leave nothing on the canvas. Its ends ARE on screen, so it is asked about them straight away
the drawn line's ends are chopped flat. Compare the two ends of this line with 8-open-path
